metaDescription: Own oil or gas rights anywhere in Cleburne County, Arkansas? We evaluate legacy Fayetteville Shale fringe interests countywide and make a cash offer, title work included.
heroLead: Cleburne County sits on the fringe of the Fayetteville Shale play, with Heber Springs as its courthouse town and Greers Ferry Lake as its economic center of gravity.
intro: Cleburne County never became one of the headline counties of the Fayetteville Shale boom the way Faulkner and Van Buren did, but leasing activity between roughly 2005 and 2010 still reached most of the county, and a real, if more modest, base of legacy production exists here today. What makes this county distinct for mineral owners is the mix: tourism-driven land use around Greers Ferry Lake sitting directly on top of shale-gas leasehold that most owners have never thought much about.

If you own an interest anywhere in Cleburne County, from Heber Springs itself out to the smaller communities like Concord, Drasco, Edgemont, Greers Ferry, or Higden, we evaluate it against actual county-wide production data and current operator activity rather than a blanket assumption about what Fayetteville Shale acreage is worth.

sections.heading: Where Cleburne County sits in the Fayetteville Shale play
paragraphs: The Fayetteville Shale's most productive rock runs through Faulkner and Van Buren counties, with Cleburne County sitting toward the eastern and southeastern fringe of that trend. Well density here has always been lower, and the wells that were drilled generally produced at more modest initial rates than the play's core. That's not a knock on the county, it's just the honest geological starting point for any valuation conversation.

Operators leased broadly across the county during the boom years regardless of exactly how good the rock was going to turn out to be, which means a meaningful share of Cleburne County acreage carries an old lease with no well ever drilled on it. If that's your situation, we treat it as undeveloped mineral acreage, a real asset, but a different one than a producing royalty interest.

sections.heading: Operator history and who's actually running legacy wells today
paragraphs: Southwestern Energy, through its SEECO subsidiary, was the dominant original developer across the Fayetteville Shale, including whatever wells were drilled in Cleburne County. Southwestern sold its Fayetteville Shale position to Flywheel Energy in 2018, and Flywheel's assets were acquired by BKV Corporation in 2021. If your royalty statements have changed the operator name over the years, or if you're not sure who currently operates a well tied to your interest, that history explains most of the confusion we see from owners in this county.
We check current operator and production filings directly with the state before making an offer, rather than relying on whatever name last appeared on a statement that may be years old.

sections.heading: Greers Ferry Lake, resort development, and mineral severance
paragraphs: A meaningful share of Cleburne County's economy runs through tourism and lake-area real estate around Greers Ferry, including the Fairfield Bay community that spans into Van Buren County. Because so much of this land has changed hands for residential and recreational purposes, mineral rights here don't always track cleanly with surface ownership the way they do on land that's stayed in one family's hands. Some lake-area lots were sold with minerals reserved by a prior owner or developer; others carried the full mineral estate along with the surface.

Before assuming you own minerals under a lake-area property, or assuming you don't, it's worth checking the actual deed history. We do that as a standard part of evaluating any Cleburne County interest, since guessing in either direction can lead an owner to walk away from a real asset or waste time pursuing one that isn't there.

sections.heading: Cleburne County Circuit Clerk records and confirming ownership
paragraphs: The Circuit Clerk's office in Heber Springs holds the county's recorded deeds, oil and gas leases, probate filings, and division orders. Because many Cleburne County mineral interests have passed through two or three generations without a formal partition, several family members frequently hold an undivided fractional share of the same tract without a clear written record of who owns exactly what percentage.

We use the Circuit Clerk's index to reconstruct that chain of title as part of any offer, working from a deed, an old lease, a probate reference, or in some cases just a family name if that's all an owner has. You're welcome to verify our research independently at the courthouse; we're not asking anyone to take our word for it on something as important as their family's mineral ownership.

faqs.question: Is Cleburne County part of the productive core of the Fayetteville Shale, or more of a fringe area?
faqs.answer: It's on the fringe. The play's most productive rock runs through Faulkner and Van Buren counties, and well density and output in Cleburne County have generally been lower and more variable.

faqs.question: Why does the operator name on my royalty statement keep changing?
faqs.answer: Most Fayetteville Shale positions in this area were originally developed by Southwestern Energy, sold to Flywheel Energy in 2018, and then acquired by BKV Corporation in 2021. A name change on your statement usually reflects one of those transactions, not a problem with your interest.

faqs.question: Our family owns a lake-area lot near Greers Ferry or Fairfield Bay. Do we have mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific deed history for your lot. Some development-era sales reserved minerals for a prior owner; others conveyed the full estate. We check your chain of title to confirm before assuming either way.

faqs.question: What if our lease from the Fayetteville Shale boom years never resulted in a drilled well?
faqs.answer: You'd own unleased or undeveloped minerals rather than an active producing royalty. That's still a real asset, priced based on nearby activity and formation potential, and we're direct about the distinction when we make an offer.

faqs.question: Several relatives inherited a share of the same interest together. Can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can confirm each person's fractional share through Cleburne County Circuit Clerk records and purchase individual shares without requiring the entire family to sell at the same time.
